Hi Samir / Leah —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time and for walking us through your ingestion pipeline and where you want to add LLM-powered summarization. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Demo summary: we showed Hosted API quickstart (text generation + streaming), embeddings for retrieval, and the per-route observability in the console.
- Your priorities: low-latency user-facing summaries, PHI-scrubbing before storage, and predictable unit costs for Q3 pilot.
- Open qualification items: expected sustained throughput (req/s and tokens/mo), any regulatory constraints (PHI/PCI/HIPAA), and whether you need on-prem/VPC isolation or can start on Hosted.

For the Hosted evaluation we typically provide:
- Quickstart guide (attached) with curl + SDK samples, sample prompt templates, and a pre-provisioned api key for a 14-day eval.
- Default rate-limit profile for trials and how to request higher burst limits.

Action items / next steps:
1) Can you share an estimate for expected concurrency and monthly tokens for the pilot? (e.g., 100 concurrent users, ~5M tokens/mo)
2) Confirm whether any PHI will be processed in the pilot (this affects whether we recommend Private + dedicated encryption/contracting).
3) If Hosted looks fine, we can spin up a trial API key and a small demo account today — who should I provision it to?

I've attached the quickstart guide and a rate limits matrix for reference. Aditya (cc) will follow up with the exact endpoints and sample rate-limit numbers.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation follow-up / Deployment mode qualification

Hi Samir — thanks for the details. Quick answers and some concrete guidance so you can assess Hosted vs Dedicated/Private for the pilot.

1) Trial rate limits (Hosted API):
   - Default trial profile: 60 requests/sec, 300 concurrent token generation streams (soft limits).
   - Burst behavior: short bursts up to 120 req/s for ~30s are typically allowed; sustained increases require a request.
   - Token-rate: depends on model; typical throughput for text-gen (redwood-medium) is ~200 tokens/sec per stream on our hosted fleet. If you plan 200 concurrent batch runs at 2k tokens each, factor the aggregate token/sec.

2) Streaming support: yes — Hosted supports chunked HTTP streaming and WebSocket-style streaming via the /v1/stream endpoint. Use the SDK or curl with "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" for partial updates.

3) IP allowlist & compliance: we can add IP allowlisting for the trial key and provide a standard DPA + HIPAA addendum template. Note: for unattended PHI processing at scale we typically recommend Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) combined with our contractual BAAs. Hosted can work for short evals if you implement a pre-processing scrubbing step as you mentioned.

Hosted vs Dedicated/Private guidance (very high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, lowest ops overhead. Good for pilots up to ~5–10M tokens/mo and moderate concurrency (<200 sustained reqs/s).
- Dedicated capacity: recommended when you need predictable sustained throughput (>200 req/s sustained) or guaranteed throughput SLAs. Also a good fit when cost per token at scale matters and you want reserved GPU pools.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workloads with PHI/PCI at scale, strict data residency, or when a customer needs customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integration.

Quickstart / sample endpoints:
- REST generation: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  Sample curl:
  curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_TRIAL_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"Summarize the clinical note:","max_tokens":256}'

- Streaming: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream

- Embeddings: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

Provisioning: Marissa, I can provision the trial key to samir.patel@acmehealth.com today and add an IP allowlist entry if you provide the source IP ranges.

I've attached a short rate limits matrix that shows our default trial and Dedicated profiles. For your numbers (3–6M tokens/mo + occasional 200 concurrent spikes) Hosted is a reasonable place to start; if you see sustained 200+ req/s over a week we should talk Dedicated.

Let us know preferred time for a 30-min tech setup and we'll provision & walk through the console, keys, and a sample prompt test.

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
